text: An electron revolving in $n^{\text{th}}$ Bohr orbit has magnetic moment $μ_{n}$. If $μ_{n}\propto n^{x}$, the value of $x$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The revolving electron is a current $I=\dfrac{ev}{2πr}$ enclosing area $πr^{2}$, so

$μ_{n}=Iπr^{2}=\dfrac{evr}{2}=\dfrac{e}{2m}(mvr)$

Bohr's quantisation condition gives $mvr=\dfrac{nh}{2π}$, so

$μ_{n}=\dfrac{neh}{4πm}=nμ_{B}$

Thus $μ_{n}\propto n^{1}$ and $x=1$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text: An alternating voltage $V(t)=220\sin 100πt$ volt is applied to a purely resistive load of $50\Omega$. The time taken for the current to rise from half of the peak value to the peak value is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a purely resistive load the current is in phase with the voltage, so $i=i_{0}\sin 100πt$ with $ω=100π\text{rad s}^{-1}$; the value of $R$ only fixes $i_{0}$.

The current is half the peak when $\sin 100πt_{1}=\dfrac{1}{2}$, i.e. $100πt_{1}=\dfrac{π}{6}$, and equals the peak when $100πt_{2}=\dfrac{π}{2}$.

$t_{2}-t_{1}=\dfrac{\dfrac{π}{2}-\dfrac{π}{6}}{100π}=\dfrac{π/3}{100π}=\dfrac{1}{300}\text{s}\approx 3.3\text{ms}$

This is $\dfrac{T}{6}$ of the period $T=\dfrac{2π}{ω}=20\text{ms}$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text: A block of mass $m$ is placed on a surface having vertical cross-section given by $y=x^{2}/4$. If coefficient of friction is 0.5, the maximum height above the ground at which block can be placed without slipping is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
On the surface $y=\dfrac{x^{2}}{4}$, the slope at any point is $\tan θ=\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{x}{2}$.

The block stays at rest where the weight component along the surface does not exceed limiting friction: $mg\sin θ\leq μmg\cos θ$, i.e. $\tan θ\leq μ$.

The highest such point has $\dfrac{x}{2}=0.5\Rightarrow x=1\text{m}$.

Its height is $y=\dfrac{(1)^{2}}{4}=\dfrac{1}{4}\text{m}$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text: When a potential difference $V$ is applied across a wire of resistance $R$, it dissipates energy at a rate $W$. If the wire is cut into two halves and these halves are connected mutually parallel across the same supply, the energy dissipation rate will become:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the whole wire across the supply, $W=\dfrac{V^{2}}{R}$.

Resistance is proportional to length, so each half has resistance $\dfrac{R}{2}$.

The two halves in parallel give

$R^{'}=\dfrac{\frac{R}{2}\times \frac{R}{2}}{\frac{R}{2}+\frac{R}{2}}=\dfrac{R}{4}$

With the same supply voltage $V$,

$W^{'}=\dfrac{V^{2}}{R^{'}}=\dfrac{V^{2}}{R/4}=4\dfrac{V^{2}}{R}=4W$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text:
Match List I with List II

  
    
    List I
    
    List II
  

  
    (A)
    Gauss's law of magnetostatics
    (I)
    $\int ⃗{E}\cdot ⃗{d}a=\frac{1}{ε_{0}}\int ρdV$
  
  
    (B)
    Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction
    (II)
    $\int ⃗{B}\cdot ⃗{d}a=0$
  
  
    (C)
    Ampere's law
    (III)
    $\int ⃗{E}\cdot ⃗{d}l=\frac{-d}{dt}\int ⃗{B}\cdot ⃗{d}a$
  
  
    (D)
    Gauss's law of electrostatics
    (IV)
    $\int ⃗{B}\cdot ⃗{d}l=μ_{0}I$
  

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let's identify each law listed in List I and match it with the corresponding mathematical expression listed in List II.

Gauss's law of magnetostatics states that the total magnetic flux through a closed surface is zero, as magnetic monopoles do not exist. This is given by the formula:

$\int ⃗{B}\cdot ⃗{da}=0$

So, (A) matches with (II).

Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction states that the induced electromotive force (emf) in any closed loop is equal to the negative of the time rate of change of the magnetic flux through the loop. It is given by:

$\int ⃗{E}\cdot ⃗{dl}=-\frac{d}{dt}\int ⃗{B}\cdot ⃗{da}$

Hence, (B) matches with (III).

Ampere's law relates the integrated magnetic field around a closed loop to the electric current passing through the loop. The mathematical expression given in the context of magnetostatics (without the displacement current) is:

$\int ⃗{B}\cdot ⃗{dl}=μ_{0}I$

Consequently, (C) matches with (IV).

Lastly, Gauss's law of electrostatics states that the total electric flux out of a closed surface is proportional to the charge enclosed within the surface:

$\int ⃗{E}\cdot ⃗{da}=\frac{1}{ε_{0}}\int ρdV$

Therefore, (D) matches with (I).

Based on these matches, the correct answer must link A-II, B-III, C-IV, and D-I:

The correct option is:

Option C

A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text: In a nuclear fission reaction of an isotope of mass $M$, three similar daughter nuclei of same mass are formed. The speed of a daughter nucleus in terms of mass defect $\Delta M$ will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Each of the three identical daughter nuclei has mass $\dfrac{M}{3}$, and by symmetry all three move with the same speed $v$.

The energy equivalent of the mass defect appears as their total kinetic energy:

$\Delta Mc^{2}=3\times \frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{M}{3}\right )v^{2}=\frac{1}{2}Mv^{2}$

$v=c\sqrt{\frac{2\Delta M}{M}}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text:
A particle of charge '$-q$' and mass '$m$' moves in a circle of radius '$r$' around an infinitely long line charge of linear charge density '$+λ$'. Then time period will be given as :

(Consider $k$ as Coulomb's constant)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The field of an infinite line charge at distance $r$ is $E=\dfrac{2kλ}{r}$, directed away from the line, so the charge $-q$ is pulled towards the line with force

$F=\dfrac{2kλq}{r}$

This attraction supplies the centripetal force for the circular motion:

$\dfrac{2kλq}{r}=mω^{2}r\Rightarrow ω^{2}=\dfrac{2kλq}{mr^{2}}$

With $ω=\dfrac{2π}{T}$:

$\dfrac{4π^{2}}{T^{2}}=\dfrac{2kλq}{mr^{2}}\Rightarrow T=2πr\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{2kλq}}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text: Two discs of moment of inertia $I_{1}=4\mathrm{kg}\mathrm{m}^{2}$ and $I_{2}=2\mathrm{kg}\mathrm{m}^{2}$, about their central axes & normal to their planes, rotating with angular speeds $10\mathrm{rad}/\mathrm{s}$ & $4\mathrm{rad}/\mathrm{s}$ respectively are brought into contact face to face with their axes of rotation coincident. The loss in kinetic energy of the system in the process is $_________ J$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the loss in kinetic energy when two spinning discs are brought together, we use the principle of conservation of angular momentum and the formula for kinetic energy. Here's how:
First, because angular momentum before and after they touch must be the same, we have:
$I_{1}ω_{1}+I_{2}ω_{2}=(I_{1}+I_{2})ω_{0}$
where:
$I_{1}$ and $I_{2}$ are the moments of inertia for the two discs.$ω_{1}$ and $ω_{2}$ are their angular speeds before contact.$ω_{0}$ is their common angular speed after contact.Plugging in the given values, we find that:
$ω_{0}=8\mathrm{rad}/\mathrm{s}$
Next, to calculate the loss in kinetic energy, we first find the total kinetic energy before and after they touch:
Before: $E_{1}=\frac{1}{2}I_{1}ω_{1}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}I_{2}ω_{2}^{2}=216\mathrm{J}$
After: $E_{2}=\frac{1}{2}(I_{1}+I_{2})ω_{0}^{2}=192\mathrm{J}$
The loss in kinetic energy ($\Delta E$) is the difference:
$\Delta E=E_{1}-E_{2}=24\mathrm{J}$
So, when the two discs are brought together, the system loses 24 J of kinetic energy.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text: A point source is emitting sound waves of intensity $16\times 10^{-8}\mathrm{Wm}^{-2}$ at the origin. The difference in intensity (magnitude only) at two points located at distances of $2m$ and $4m$ from the origin respectively will be $_________$ $\times 10^{-8}\mathrm{Wm}^{-2}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To solve this problem, we need to understand the relationship between the intensity of sound waves and the distance from the source. The intensity $I$ of sound waves from a point source decreases with the square of the distance $r$ from the source, according to the inverse square law, which can be expressed as:

$I\propto \frac{1}{r^{2}}$

This means that if the distance is doubled, the intensity becomes one-fourth of its initial value because $(2r)^{2}=4r^{2}$.

The initial intensity given at the origin (source) is:

$I_{0}=16\times 10^{-8}\mathrm{Wm}^{-2}$

Let's call $I_{1}$ the intensity at $r=2\text{m}$ and $I_{2}$ the intensity at $r=4\text{m}$. Using the inverse square law, we can write:

$I_{1}=\frac{I_{0}}{(2)^{2}}=\frac{I_{0}}{4}$

and

$I_{2}=\frac{I_{0}}{(4)^{2}}=\frac{I_{0}}{16}$

Now substitute the given value for $I_{0}$ to find $I_{1}$ and $I_{2}$:

$I_{1}=\frac{16\times 10^{-8}}{4}=4\times 10^{-8}\mathrm{Wm}^{-2}$

$I_{2}=\frac{16\times 10^{-8}}{16}=1\times 10^{-8}\mathrm{Wm}^{-2}$

Now to find the difference in intensity (magnitude only) between the two points, we subtract $I_{2}$ from $I_{1}$:

$\Delta I=|I_{1}-I_{2}|$

$\Delta I=|4\times 10^{-8}-1\times 10^{-8}|$

$\Delta I=3\times 10^{-8}\mathrm{Wm}^{-2}$

So the difference in intensity (magnitude only) at the two points is:

$3\times 10^{-8}\mathrm{Wm}^{-2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text: A vector has magnitude same as that of $⃗{A}=3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}$ and is parallel to $⃗{B}=4\hat{i}+3\hat{j}$. The $x$ and $y$ components of this vector in first quadrant are $x$ and 3 respectively where $x=$ $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find a vector that has the same magnitude as vector $⃗{A}$ and is parallel to vector $⃗{B}$, we use the formula:
$⃗{N}=|⃗{A}|\hat{B}$
First, let's find the magnitude of $⃗{A}$, which is $|⃗{A}|$.
$|⃗{A}|=\sqrt{3^{2}+4^{2}}=5$
We're given that $⃗{B}=4\hat{i}+3\hat{j}$, so to make $⃗{N}$ parallel to $⃗{B}$ and have it have the same magnitude as $⃗{A}$, they should be the same when $⃗{N}$'s magnitude is divided by 5, since $|⃗{A}|=5$.
So, $⃗{N}=\frac{5(4\hat{i}+3\hat{j})}{5}=4\hat{i}+3\hat{j}$.
This means the $x$ component of the vector in the first quadrant is 4, and the $y$ component is given as 3. So, $x=4$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift
